data.name: Hasin
data.gender_notes: Hasin is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Hasin is derived from the Arabic root h-s-n, which means 'to be content' or 'to please'. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that this name was given to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when he was born, as it reflects the joy and contentment felt by his parents upon his arrival. Hasin is a name that evokes feelings of happiness, satisfaction, and pleasure, making it an excellent choice for a child who is expected to bring joy to those around him.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the spiritual joy and contentment of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
data.etymology: Hasin belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joyful, content, pleased.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hasin total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hasin holds a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. In many Muslim societies, the naming of a child is considered an important event, often reflecting the parents' hopes, dreams, and aspirations for their offspring. The name Hasin, which connotes happiness, contentment, and pleasure, is believed to bring positive energy and good fortune to the child, as well as to those around him. Additionally, the name is often associated with the beauty and grace of nature, as the Arabic word h-s-n is also used to describe beautiful or pleasing things.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hasin holds deep significance as it reflects the inner qualities of contentment, satisfaction, and pleasure that are highly valued in Islamic teachings. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself encouraged his followers to seek happiness and contentment, as he said, "The believer's shade on the Day of Resurrection will be his charity, and his smiling in the face of misfortune will be his entrance to Paradise." (Tirmidhi) By bestowing the name Hasin upon a child, parents are invoking the blessings of contentment, joy, and pleasure, not just for their child, but also for themselves and the wider community. Furthermore, the name Ismail, which is also derived from the same Arabic root, is the name of Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham's) beloved son and the ancestor of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself, further strengthening the spiritual significance of this name in Islamic tradition.
